name: Pearl Global Industries Ltd
title: Pearl Global Industries Ltd - 532808 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Pearl Global H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31.1% to INR3,330 crores, with Q2 PAT at a record INR126 crores.
summary.overview: Pearl Global reported record H1 and Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue, adjusted EBITDA and PAT, with Q2 revenue up 37.2% YoY to INR1,802 crores. Growth was helped by a catch-up in US sourcing after a conservative prior year, FTA-led interest from UK and EU buyers, and a one-time net tariff gain of about INR10 crores plus INR98 crores of value-added services that management says are not part of the run-rate. Working capital days rose to 56 as receivable days moved from 30 to 50 on late-quarter shipments and deferred factoring, which management expects to normalise over the next two quarters. Management reiterated INR6,000 crore+ revenue in FY27 and a 12-14% EBITDA margin trajectory, while flagging Bangladesh wage revision risk.

segments.name: US market
segments.commentary: US is the largest market at roughly half of revenue; retailers kept inventories lean into a compressed Thanksgiving-to-Christmas window (Thanksgiving on 26 Nov, selling window about 12-12.5% shorter).

segments.name: UK and Canada
segments.commentary: Management cites strong growth in Canada and UK; UK volumes rose after the India-UK FTA took effect on 15 July 2026.

segments.name: EU, Japan, Australia
segments.commentary: EU volumes are inching up with elevated interest ahead of an FTA expected by early FY28; Japan and Australia volumes were steady.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98 crores against expenses of INR96.5 crores (about 1.5% EBITDA margin); management says this was a holiday-season customer-retention service and not included in forecasts.

segments.name: Vietnam and Indonesia
segments.commentary: Vietnam is growing steadily with premium customers and is driving the realisation gain; Indonesia is growing from a much lower base. Management said these two geographies drove the higher average realisation.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Management is working to stabilise operations and reach breakeven; no figures were given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue of INR6,000 crores or more, which management says is achievable within this financial year based on the Q3 order book; this is described as value-based and volume is unguided.
EBITDA margin trajectory of 12-14% through FY30, announced at the September 2026 Investor Day; management says H1 results are progressing in that direction.
Receivable days expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27, improving free cash flow in H2 FY27.
Management is not forecasting the tariff refund or net tariff gain going forward, but says further partnership-related gains are possible.
Tax rate guidance of around 15% blended on a long-term basis.
Bangladesh wage revision: management expects a rise to a range of about 15-18k taka and says some of the increase is already in its costing for Q3 and Q4.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: new 7 million pieces per year manufacturing unit inaugurated in Q2; about 20% operational as of the call and expected to reach full capacity over 6-8 months. Washing laundry started in September.

Bangladesh backward integration: knitting and processing unit with capex of INR350-375 crores (INR200 crores approved by board), processing operational by early 2028; first 10 tonne knitting phase has started.
CWIP of INR225 crores at 30 Sep 2026, mainly Bangladesh, expected to be capitalised in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Capacity-expansion capex of INR325-350 crores across geographies, of which INR100 crores to be capitalised in FY27; the remainder is under evaluation, with some for Vietnam and Indonesia.
Total capitalisation of INR900-950 crores over FY27-FY30, expected to be complete by FY29 or earlier. Management says the INR225 crore CWIP was approved in FY26 and is part of this total.
India utilisation at about 68-69% in H1; the new Bihar plant is ramping up with hiring and training. Haryana has four factories.
demand_pricing: US retailers are keeping inventories lean into peak season; management sees no big change in inventory planning, with the mix shifting between national brands and private label.
Management cites a shift of sourcing from Turkey and China toward India, Bangladesh and Vietnam under the new FTAs and tariff diversification.

Sea freight peaked at about USD12,500 per container in the August-October season versus a normal USD2,000-3,000, which management says reduced spot container availability; Pearl used its spot rates for value-added logistics help to select customers.

Average realisation rose on a 7-8% INR depreciation against the USD and on product mix (knits and premium products); management says the net gain is lower than the currency move because costs also convert. A slight realisation improvement was seen in Bangladesh as well.
Management says cost inflation is passed through to customers in the next season's pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Are US brands restocking now that tariffs are partly resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retailers stayed cautious with lean inventory ahead of peak season, with no big change in inventory planning. Pearl's volumes rose because it serves both national brands and private label.

qa_highlights.question: What wage increase is expected in Bangladesh and will margins be hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a minimum wage rise to about 15-18k taka (about 15%, possibly a bit more), from around 13,000 taka today. It said the wage is not the main cost driver and that currency depreciation and productivity should offset much of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H1 run-rate sustainable and is there cost or freight pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the surge reflects pent-up sourcing after a weak FY26 (growth below 9%) and FTA tailwinds, and it is too early to project FY28 growth. It did not give a clear answer on cost inflation beyond passing raw material changes to customers in the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the value-added services line and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR98 crores was a holiday-season service and it is not factored into forecasts. Removing it from revenue and its ~INR1.5 crore EBITDA leaves the margin roughly unchanged, and continuation is not foreseen in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net tariff gain and is more expected?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10 crores of net tariff adjustment was booked this quarter from partnership discussions with customers, who shared the tariff cost. Management is not forecasting a refund, but more partnership-related gains are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR6,000 crore+ target consistent with H1 growth of 30%+, implying a sharp H2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees a strong order book for Q3 and that Q4 bookings are still building, with no slowdown visible yet. It did not reconcile the implied H2 growth rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India capacity utilisation only 68-69%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UK and EU buyers want to ramp in Bangladesh first and add one or two programmes in India later. Bihar is still hiring and training, and utilisation may end the year somewhat higher.

risks_watch: Bangladesh minimum wage revision (expected by early December, arrears in January) and possible unrest: management says two days were lost across three factories and all five own factories were fully running as of the call.
Receivables: receivable days rose from 30 to 50 and working capital days to 56; normalisation expected in Q3 and Q4, and the free cash flow effect depends on it.
Haryana wage increase of 35% and PF adjustment, plus Karnataka wage pressure (garment exempted for now), which affect India margins.
Dependence on the FY27 INR6,000 crore+ revenue target, which implies a sharp slowdown in H2 growth relative to H1's 30%+.
Value-added services and the net tariff gain (about INR11.5 crores in total) are non-recurring and not included in forecasts.
Gasoline price path (management's threshold is USD4 per gallon) and US consumer spending; an inventory-led slowdown in the US is a risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FTA-driven order flow, but cautious on near-term cash conversion and forward volume, which management declined to project. Management was open about the Bangladesh wage risk but framed it as manageable, and gave few specifics on value-added services and tariff gains beyond saying they are not run-rate.
key_quotes: We are one of those few established company who can serve them from both the countries.
Both these will get normalized within this year itself, within this next two quarters.
Pulkit, we are not seeing such a slowdown as of yet. If that's the question you are asking.

adds.what: 7 million pieces/yr Bangladesh manufacturing unit (inaugurated Q2, ~20% operational, full capacity over 6-8 months)
Bangladesh knitting and processing unit (backward integration; processing operational by early 2028, first 10 tonne knitting phase started)
Capacity-expansion capex across geographies (INR100 cr to be capitalised in FY27; remainder under evaluation, some for Vietnam and Indonesia)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue of INR6,000 crore+ (value basis, volume unguided), backed by a Q3 order book and Bangladesh capacity ramp, but about INR98 crore of one-off value-added services and a tariff gain flatter the quarter, and no volume figures were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 10.5% in H1 (up 120 bps) and 12-14% is the FY30 roadmap, but value-added services (INR98 cr at ~1.5% margin) and a ~INR10 cr tariff gain are non-recurring, and Bangladesh wages rise ~15-18% from ~13,000 taka with only part already costed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangladesh 7 mn pieces/yr unit is inaugurated and ~20% operational, reaching full capacity over 6-8 months, and INR225 cr CWIP is to be capitalised in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 order book is strong and FY27 revenue of INR6,000 cr+ is reaffirmed (H1 revenue INR3,330 cr, up 31.1%), but volume is unguided and the H2 slowdown implied by the target is not reconciled.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India utilisation is only 68-69% and the INR325-350 cr capacity-expansion capex is mostly still under evaluation, so the remainder is likely to be firmed up, with the Bangladesh knitting unit (INR350-375 cr) already approved in part (INR200 cr).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue of INR6,000 cr+ was raised in tone, but H1 growth of 31% is flattered by about INR108 cr of one-offs (VAS INR98 cr plus tariff gain ~INR10 cr) and management declined to project H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivable days rose from 30 to 50 and working capital days to 56, the Bangladesh wage revision lands by early December, and the INR6,000 cr target implies a sharp H2 slowdown from H1's 30%+ growth.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise from 50 to 30-type levels
rows.why: Receivable days rose from 30 to 50 and management expects normalisation in Q3 and Q4 FY27, which would free cash flow in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Cost pass-through to next-season pricing
rows.why: Management says cost inflation is passed to customers in next season's pricing, and INR depreciation of 7-8% lifted average realisation.

rows.label: UK and EU FTA-led sourcing shift
rows.why: India-UK FTA took effect on 15 July 2026 with UK volumes rising, and EU FTA expected by early FY28 with elevated buyer interest.

tone.note: Management was confident on FTA-led order flow, the INR6,000 cr target and the Bangladesh ramp, but cautious on cash conversion and H2 volume; analysts pressed on the H2 slowdown implied by the target and on the one-off nature of VAS and tariff gains.

oneOffs.what: INR98 cr value-added services revenue (holiday-season customer-retention service, not in forecasts) at ~1.5% margin, inflating Q2 revenue growth
About INR10-11.5 cr net tariff gain booked this quarter from customer partnership discussions, non-recurring, flatters EBITDA and PAT
Catch-up in US sourcing after a conservative prior year (FY26 growth below 9%) and pent-up demand, plus late-quarter shipments

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37.2% to INR1,802 cr, but the brief flags INR98 cr of non-recurring value-added services (about 5% of the quarter's revenue, roughly 1.5% margin) and a ~INR10 cr tariff gain, and attributes part of growth to a catch-up in US sourcing after a weak FY26; receivable days rising from 30 to 50 also means some revenue is not yet cash-backed.
